analysis: Examined the five changed source files and their tests. (1) EngineV2KVBackendPolicy.swift:37-41 adds the exact ID "RecursiveSI/flint-int4" to the auto-paged list. Auto selection stays exact-match only, and the kill switch (DARKBLOOM_CBV2_PAGED_KV), the VLM veto, the degrade-on-failure path and the crash-loop guard are unchanged. The test at EngineV2KVBackendPolicyTests.swift:31 confirms the prefix cache stays off by default for this ID, so there is no new at-rest surface under T-041. (2) FlintNativeProtocolConstraint.swift:152-162 adds maskCacheKey, which returns the interned state id when the state is known, the budget is positive and the constraint is not exhausted. It also adds allowsChainedDecode=true. State ids are append-only and never reused, so the key-to-mask mapping is stable. The allowed set depends on the budget only via remainingTokens>0, which the key guard enforces. The exhausted and unknown cases return nil, so nothing is cached and the fail-closed empty mask is preserved. (3) FlintAnswerStopConstraint.swift:70-91 maps matched nodes to key -1 and scanning nodes to the base state key. The base state key is always non-negative, so it cannot collide with -1. The mask depends only on the base state, so stop progress does not change the mask. Reads happen under the lock, and the base is called after the lock is released, as before. Residual question: the consumer of maskCacheKey and allowsChainedDecode (the CBv2 sampler) is not in the supplied diff. Per-request scoping of the mask cache, cache invalidation, and whether speculative chained decode discards state correctly cannot be verified here. If a mask cache were shared across requests with different constraint instances, state ids could collide; that cache and its scoping are outside the supplied evidence. This is relevant to TB-007, T-028 and the integrity of constrained output. The tests add a keys-follow-masks check but do not cover cross-request isolation. No concrete regression is identified in the supplied lines.
